id.description: Unique within the corpus; a runner reports failures by it.

input.description: The expression exactly as a user would type it. It is never trimmed or normalised before parsing, and spans index into it.

options.description: ParseOptions. Omitting `dialect` exercises dialect detection; omitting `timezone` means UTC.

expect.description: The whole Schedule the parse returns, compared in full: every field with its raw, span, terms, values and star, plus the optional macro, trailing and candidates. An optional key absent here must be absent there.

expectSummary.description: A partial expectation, for cases where the whole Schedule would be noise. `dialect` is always compared. `candidates` and `unsupported` are compared exactly, and absent here means absent (or empty) there. `values` and `star` compare only the fields they name.

unsupported.description: Names of the fields holding at least one term marked unsupported, in field order.

values.description: Field name to its exact Field.values.

star.description: Field name to its exact Field.star.

expectError.description: The ParseError the parse returns instead. Parsing never throws and never returns a partial schedule.

code.description: Closed list. A code means no Term could be built; a token this dialect merely does not support is not an error (see tokens in dialect.schema.json).

span.description: [start, end) character offsets into `input`, as UTF-16 code units. A port whose strings are bytes or code points must convert.

provenance.description: Where the expected values come from. `spec` = the dialect specification or documented behaviour; `derived` = read from reference source, with `source` citing the section; `assumed` = the platform's documentation is silent and this is the behaviour the corpus chose; `source` cites the DERIVATION entry that records the silence and the reason; `captured` = recorded from a running reference implementation, with `platform` and `recording`.
